speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned episodes of unresponsiveness with facial grimacing; how long does each episode typically last, and do you lose consciousness?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Absence Epilepsy (Childhood Absence Seizures).

The clinical picture of a 7-year-old with recurrent staring spells lasting 3-4 minutes, unresponsiveness, no post-ictal confusion (only lethargy), and a specific "muddy taste" is highly characteristic of childhood absence epilepsy. The duration of 3-4 minutes is unusually long for typical absence seizures, which are usually brief, but the semiology strongly points to this etiology. I will request an EEG to confirm the diagnosis and look for 3-Hz spike-and-wave discharges. REQUEST TEST: EEG
